name: Vincenzo Ciancia
title: Senior Researcher (Primo Ricercatore), CNR-ISTI, Pisa

description: Vincenzo Ciancia — Senior Researcher at CNR-ISTI, Pisa. Logic, formal verification and AI: spatial model checking, explainable medical imaging, formally supervised AI agents.
profile: I work where logic, formal verification and AI meet, with a focus on trustworthy AI that keeps a human in the loop.

I co-created spatial model checking for image analysis, a research line now in its tenth year, and have worked on all of it: metatheory (completeness, bisimilarity, minimisation), language design, high-performance execution (GPU kernels, lazy parallel evaluation, multi-level caching) and hybrid symbolic–neural AI, applied to medical imaging (brain tumours, acute ischemic stroke).

I work daily with frontier AI models and agents under formally grounded supervision, a method I turned into a tool, NAIMA. An Anthropic AI for Science Program award (2026) funds an ongoing experiment in which LLM agents produce new results in explainable, symbolic medical image segmentation.
About 1,700 citations and an h-index of 20 (Google Scholar, October 2026); our spatial logics and model checkers are cited by research groups in 16 countries.

open_problems.title: Explainable, symbolic image segmentation as accurate as neural networks
open_problems.problem: Can segmentation procedures written as readable logical specifications match the accuracy of end-to-end neural networks on medical images?
open_problems.why_hard: Hand-written symbolic procedures have long trailed neural networks in accuracy, and the space of candidate programs is large; every improvement must keep the procedure inspectable and justified, not just better-scoring.
open_problems.doing: An LLM-agent research loop that I direct proposes, runs and refines segmentation programs in the declarative language of VoxLogicA 2, each with a stated rationale and versioned for reproducibility, on public brain-tumour benchmarks. This is hybrid AI with a strong symbolic component; it is funded by the Anthropic AI for Science Program (2026).

open_problems.title: Choosing parameters without an oracle
open_problems.problem: How should the thresholds and parameters of a symbolic segmentation procedure be chosen when the ground truth of the image at hand is not available?
open_problems.why_hard: Accuracy reported with parameters tuned against ground truth is an upper bound, not a deployable result. Label-free selection criteria must be justified and must not leak information from the evaluation set.
open_problems.doing: I keep oracle-tuned and label-free results separate in every experiment, and I am studying selection criteria that depend only on the image and on properties stated in the logic.

open_problems.title: Medical AI workflows that are compliant by construction
open_problems.problem: Can the transparency, traceability and human-oversight requirements of the EU AI Act be part of an executable specification of a clinical AI workflow, rather than documentation written afterwards?
open_problems.why_hard: Regulatory requirements are stated in legal language; workflows mix neural components, symbolic reasoning and human decisions, and the guarantees must hold for every execution.
open_problems.doing: A workflow language in which human assessment is a primitive and clinical protocols are encoded directly, so that compliance properties follow from the structure of the workflow (ISoLA 2026, to appear).

open_problems.title: LLM agents guided by formal methods
open_problems.problem: How can large amounts of software produced by LLM agents be trusted when no human can read all of it?
open_problems.why_hard: Agents produce code faster than it can be reviewed; trust has to come from specifications, tests and process discipline that the agents themselves cannot bypass.
open_problems.doing: NAIMA, a fully automated, LLM-driven, parallel multi-agent project-management tool that applies established software-engineering practice and manages its own development. VoxLogicA 2 was written entirely by AI agents from a human-authored reference implementation used as an executable specification. Two publications in preparation.

open_problems.title: A formally verified, high-performance spatial model checker
open_problems.problem: Can an image-analysis engine that runs unattended for weeks be both fast and correct by construction?
open_problems.why_hard: Lazy parallel evaluation, caching and GPU kernels are where performance comes from and also where errors hide; verification and performance engineering usually pull in opposite directions.
open_problems.doing: VoxLogicA 2.1, built exclusively through NAIMA: its core is a formal model with automatically proved properties, from which high-performance implementations are derived.
